MetaCheck Report

Spinal Manipulation and Other Conservative Treatments for Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain Compared with Natural History and Sham: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis

2026-11-27 · Metacheck 0.4.4.41 · DOI 10.64898/2026.09.16.26359287

1to fix4to check0to decide by hand1fine10not applicable

To fix (1)

To fix Reproducibility Check

What we found

  • We assessed 54 R code files for reproducibility and ran 46 of them (each in an isolated Docker container).
  • 18 of 48 scripts ran without error when executed (5 more are run by another script with source()).
  • Of the others, 27 did not reproduce, 2 could not run because a package or program was not available, and 1 did not finish within the time limit.
  • 21 installable dependencies detected.
  • 340 statistics stored from the extracted output; 2 of 71 reported tests matched (2.8%).

Note

See the section Reproducibility Check below for the details.

To check (4)

To check Codebook Check

What we found

  • We parsed 118 variable definitions from codebook/README files.
  • 122 of 153 data columns (80%) are documented in a codebook; 31 are not.
  • 118 matched columns have a conflicting or ambiguous label that needs resolution.
Show details

This module checks whether each extracted data column is documented in a codebook or README, and flags documented variables that never appear in the data.

We examined 4 codebook/README/label sources and 153 data columns across 4 files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). No install.packages() calls were found in any of the code files.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 4 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

How to make your code run on another computer

We ran your code on a clean computer, the way a reader or reviewer would. Below is each problem we found, the scripts it affects, and how to fix it. Fix them in the order given: a problem near the top can cause the ones below it.

Files are missing from your deposit.

  • 0j_nh_cross_reference_v4.R reads nh_trajectory_registry.csv.
  • 00_CLINICAL_OUTPUT_FREEZE_AUDIT.R reads Clinical_Translation_Primary_Canonical.csv.

The script stops at the line that reads the file.

  1. Find the file on your computer.
  2. Add it to the deposit, in the folder where the script looks for it.
  3. If you cannot share it, for example for privacy reasons, say so in the README, and explain where readers can get it and where to put it.

A script could not open a file, but the error does not say which.

  • 0_RUN_TIMESHAPE_SENSITIVITY.R

Check every file the script reads. Make sure each one is in the deposit, and that its location is written from the top folder of the project.

A package could not be installed.

  • 0g_conventional_NMA_diagnostics.R needs BigDataStatMeth.
  • 2_Figure2_DirectIndirect_NMA.R needs BigDataStatMeth.

BigDataStatMeth could not be installed in our run. Record the versions you used (in R, renv::init() writes them to a renv.lock file) and your R version, and say in the README where any package that is not on CRAN comes from.

A script uses something it does not create or load itself.

  • 00_RDS_FRESHNESS_AUDIT.R

Usually the object was still in your R session from earlier work, or another script made it.

  1. Restart R (in RStudio: Session > Restart R).
  2. Run each script from top to bottom, and fix what is missing.
  3. If a script needs results of another, save them to a file in the first script and read them in the second.
  4. Load every package with library() at the top.

A script runs longer than our limit of 5 minutes.

  • 1_BAYES_NMA_JAGS_MODIFIED_v4_3.R

State in the README how long each script runs. If some steps take hours, save their results (such as fitted models) to files, add those to the deposit, and let the script read them, so readers can check the rest without waiting.

Metacheck can’t automatically establish what caused the error, or how it should be improved.

The code should be changed, because as written it does not find these files. The code reads files that are only inside SilverCrucible_model_outputs_v1.zip, SilverCrucible_code_v1.zip, and no script unpacks them. We unpacked them in their folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks them (such as unzip("SilverCrucible_model_outputs_v1.zip") in R), or upload the files unpacked. 26 data paths were built at runtime with sprintf()/paste()/file.path() instead of written as a literal path — this is fragile authoring practice (it silently breaks if the code is run from a different working directory than the author’s own). We resolved all of these on a best-effort basis.

Files the deposit does not hold

The scripts that did not run through read 8 data files that are not in the deposit, and no script of the deposit writes: table_nma_chronic.csv, nh_trajectories.csv, nh_recovery_probabilities.csv, nh_common_scale_expanded.csv, nh_trajectory_registry.csv, diagnostic_scale_reconciliation_acute.csv, diagnostic_scale_reconciliation_chronic.csv, table6_clinicalinterpretation.csv.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 53 scripts: 18 ran without error, 27 errored, 1 timed out, 2 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 5 were run by another script with source(). Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions. 1 script could not be tried, because a file it needs was not downloaded: 27_clinical_sanity_check.R. It is not counted as a script that did not reproduce. The file: SilverCrucible_model_outputs_v1/nma_results.rds (149 MB); files over 100 MB are not downloaded.

Dependency-unavailable errors

2 scripts could not run because their own dependency is unavailable — the package failed to install from both live CRAN and the CRAN Archive (or a GitHub/URL source could not be resolved). This is an infrastructure limitation, not a defect in the paper’s code, so it does not force the traffic light red.

File
0g_conventional_NMA_diagnostics.R
2_Figure2_DirectIndirect_NMA.R

setwd() in the code

9 scripts call setwd(). This is bad practice: it hardcodes where the code must run (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine) and breaks the moment the code is run anywhere else. To run the code we replaced these calls with a statement that does nothing. Any such script that then ran is reproducible only after ignoring a setwd() that should not have been in the code and needs to be fixed.

> caption_transitivity <- function(dat, condition, value_col, metric_label) {
>   usable <- dat %>%
>     filter(is.finite(.data[[value_col]]))
> 
>   n_comp <- n_distinct(usable$Comparison)
>   sparse <- usable %>%
>     count(Comparison, name = "n_rows") %>%
>     summarise(n = sum(n_rows < 3)) %>%
>     pull(n)
> 
>   ovs <- pairwise_overlap_summary(usable, value_col)
> 
>   medians <- usable %>%
>     group_by(Comparison) %>%
>     summarise(
>       med = median(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
>       .groups = "drop"
>     )
> 
>   spread <- if (nrow(medians) >= 2) {
>     max(medians$med, na.rm = TRUE) -
>       min(medians$med, na.rm = TRUE)
>   } else {
>     NA_real_
>   }
> 
>   overlap_sentence <- case_when(
>     !is.finite(ovs$median_overlap) ~
>       "Too few non-sparse pairwise comparisons were available to summarize overlap reliably.",
>     ovs$median_overlap >= 0.35 ~
>       "The middle 50% of the distributions overlaps appreciably across many pairwise comparisons.",
>     ovs$median_overlap >= 0.10 ~
>       "Overlap is mixed: some pairwise comparisons occupy similar ranges, whereas others are separated.",
>     TRUE ~
>       "The middle 50% of the distributions shows little overlap across many pairwise comparisons."
>   )
> 
>   paste0(
>     condition, " network only; no acute-versus-chronic comparison is intended. ",
>     "The figure includes ", n_comp, " randomized pairwise comparison",
>     ifelse(n_comp == 1, "", "s"), ". ",
>     overlap_sentence, " ",
>     "The range of comparison-specific medians is approximately ",
>     fmt_num(spread, 1), " ", metric_label, ". ",
>     sparse, " comparison", ifelse(sparse == 1, " is", "s are"),
>     " represented by fewer than three arm-time observations; single-line boxes ",
>     "should therefore be read as sparse evidence rather than stable distributions. ",
>     "Multi-arm trials may contribute to more than one pairwise row. ",
>     "This is a descriptive transitivity assessment and does not establish the assumption by itself."
>   )
> }

> cat("No external NH values enter the internal fit.\n")
No external NH values enter the internal fit.
> fit_at_lambda <- function(dd,lambda,interaction=FALSE) {
>   dd <- droplevels(dd); dd$h <- 1-exp(-lambda*dd$time)
>   if(nlevels(dd$Treatment)<2) return(NULL)
>   contrasts(dd$Treatment) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Treatment))
>   form <- if(interaction) g_raw ~ h*Treatment else g_raw ~ h+Treatment
>   tryCatch(nlme::lme(
>     fixed=form, random=~1|study, data=dd,
>     weights=nlme::varFixed(~I(1/wt)), method="ML",
>     control=nlme::lmeControl(msMaxIter=200,opt="optim",returnObject=TRUE), na.action=na.omit
>   ),error=function(e) NULL)
> }
> profile_phase <- function(dd,phase) {
>   # Broad log grid. No 0.90 asymptote or external lambda is supplied.
>   grid <- if(phase=="Acute") exp(seq(log(0.003),log(2.0),length.out=70)) else exp(seq(log(0.0005),log(0.30),length.out=70))
>   prof <- lapply(grid,function(lam){
>     m<-fit_at_lambda(dd,lam,FALSE)
>     if(is.null(m)) return(tibble(lambda=lam,AIC=Inf,logLik=NA_real_))
>     tibble(lambda=lam,AIC=AIC(m),logLik=as.numeric(logLik(m)))
>   }) %>% bind_rows()
>   if(!any(is.finite(prof$AIC))) stop(phase,": all internal common-trajectory fits failed.")
>   best_lam <- prof$lambda[which.min(prof$AIC)]
>   common <- fit_at_lambda(dd,best_lam,FALSE)
>   dev <- fit_at_lambda(dd,best_lam,TRUE)
>   list(lambda=best_lam,profile=prof,common=common,deviation=dev)
> }
> extract_common <- function(fitobj,phase,display_cap,nh_phase) {
>   b <- nlme::fixef(fitobj$common); V <- vcov(fitobj$common)
>   if(!all(c("(Intercept)","h") %in% names(b))) stop(phase,": expected internal coefficients missing.")
>   g0 <- unname(b["(Intercept)"]); A <- unname(b["h"]); lam <- fitobj$lambda
>   grid <- tibble(Condition=phase,week=seq(0,display_cap,length.out=401)) %>%
>     mutate(h=1-exp(-lam*week),g_internal=g0+A*h,p_internal=pnorm(g_internal),
>            g_external=nh_phase$g0_mu+nh_phase$A_mu*(1-exp(-nh_phase$lam_mu*week)),p_external=pnorm(g_external))
>   # Approximate fixed-effect CI for the common temporal component.
>   V2 <- V[c("(Intercept)","h"),c("(Intercept)","h"),drop=FALSE]
>   X <- cbind(1,grid$h); se <- sqrt(pmax(0,rowSums((X%*%V2)*X)))
>   grid <- grid %>% mutate(g_internal_lo=g_internal-1.96*se,g_internal_hi=g_internal+1.96*se,
>                           p_internal_lo=pnorm(g_internal_lo),p_internal_hi=pnorm(g_internal_hi))
>   pars <- tibble(Condition=phase,internal_g0=g0,internal_A=A,internal_lambda=lam,
>                  implied_p_start=pnorm(g0),implied_p_asymptote=pnorm(g0+A),
>                  external_g0=nh_phase$g0_mu,external_A=nh_phase$A_mu,external_lambda=nh_phase$lam_mu,
>                  external_p_asymptote=pnorm(nh_phase$g0_mu+nh_phase$A_mu))
>   list(grid=grid,pars=pars)
> }
> model_test <- function(fitobj,phase) {
>   common<-fitobj$common; dev<-fitobj$deviation
>   if(is.null(dev)) return(tibble(Condition=phase,lambda_profiled=fitobj$lambda,AIC_common=AIC(common),AIC_treatment_shape=NA_real_,delta_AIC=NA_real_,LRT=NA_real_,df=NA_real_,p=NA_real_))
>   aa<-tryCatch(anova(common,dev),error=function(e)NULL)
>   if(is.null(aa)||nrow(aa)<2) return(tibble(Condition=phase,lambda_profiled=fitobj$lambda,AIC_common=AIC(common),AIC_treatment_shape=AIC(dev),delta_AIC=AIC(dev)-AIC(common),LRT=NA_real_,df=NA_real_,p=NA_real_))
>   tibble(Condition=phase,lambda_profiled=fitobj$lambda,AIC_common=AIC(common),AIC_treatment_shape=AIC(dev),delta_AIC=AIC(dev)-AIC(common),
>          LRT=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(aa$L.Ratio[2])),df=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(aa$df[2]-aa$df[1])),p=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(aa$`p-value`[2])))
> }
> loo_treatment <- function(dd,phase,lambda,ref_grid) {
>   out<-list()
>   for(tx in levels(droplevels(dd$Treatment))) {
>     dx<-droplevels(filter(dd,as.character(Treatment)!=tx))
>     m<-fit_at_lambda(dx,lambda,FALSE)
>     if(is.null(m)) {out[[tx]]<-tibble(Condition=phase,Left_out=tx,status="fit failed");next}
>     b<-nlme::fixef(m); if(!all(c("(Intercept)","h")%in%names(b))) next
>     g<-unname(b["(Intercept)"])+unname(b["h"])*(1-exp(-lambda*ref_grid$week))
>     p<-pnorm(g)
>     out[[tx]]<-tibble(Condition=phase,Left_out=tx,status="ok",max_abs_pp=100*max(abs(p-ref_grid$p_internal),na.rm=TRUE),mean_abs_pp=100*mean(abs(p-ref_grid$p_internal),na.rm=TRUE))
>   }
>   bind_rows(out)
> }
> results<-list()
> grids<-list()
> pars<-list()
> tests<-list()
> loos<-list()
> profiles<-list()
> for(phase in c("Acute","Chronic")) {
>   dd<-filter(d,Condition==phase)
>   display_cap<-ifelse(phase=="Acute",26,54)
>   nhp<-if(phase=="Acute")nh$acute else nh$chronic
>   fitobj<-profile_phase(dd,phase)
>   ex<-extract_common(fitobj,phase,display_cap,nhp)
>   grids[[phase]]<-ex$grid; pars[[phase]]<-ex$pars; tests[[phase]]<-model_test(fitobj,phase)
>   loos[[phase]]<-loo_treatment(dd,phase,fitobj$lambda,ex$grid)
>   profiles[[phase]]<-fitobj$profile %>% mutate(Condition=phase,.before=1)
>   results[[phase]]<-fitobj
> }

> model_string <- "
> model {
>   for (i in 1:N) {
>     # External population-mean NH is fixed at its Bayesian posterior mean.
>     # Pointwise external NH posterior variance enters the likelihood variance.
>     y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],
>                  pow(se[i]*se[i] + nh_var[i] + sigma2_resid, -1))
> 
>     mu[i] <- nh_mean[i]
>              + beta_n * size_c[i]
>              + beta_q * pedro_c[i]
>              + tx_effect[tx[i]]
>              + is_smt[i] * gamma[smt_prov[i]]
>              + u[study[i]]
>              + v[tx[i],study[i]]
>   }
> 
>   beta_n ~ dnorm(0,pow(1,-2))
>   beta_q ~ dnorm(0,pow(1,-2))
> 
>   sigma_tx ~ dt(0,pow(0.5,-2),1) T(0,)
>   for (k in 1:n_tx) {
>     tx_effect[k] ~ dnorm(0,pow(sigma_tx,-2))
>   }
> 
>   for (p in 1:n_smt_prov) {
>     z_gamma[p] ~ dnorm(0,1)
>     gamma[p] <- z_gamma[p] * sigma_prov
>   }
>   sigma_prov ~ dt(0,pow(0.5,-2),1) T(0,)
> 
>   for (j in 1:n_study) {
>     u[j] ~ dnorm(0,pow(tau,-2))
>   }
>   tau ~ dt(0,pow(0.5,-2),1) T(0,)
> 
>   # Non-centered treatment-by-study random effects.
>   # This is the same hierarchical model, reparameterized to avoid the
>   # near-zero variance funnel that caused slow mixing of sigma_tx_x_study.
>   for (k in 1:n_tx) {
>     for (j in 1:n_study) {
>       z_v[k,j] ~ dnorm(0,1)
>       v[k,j] <- z_v[k,j] * sigma_tx_x_study
>     }
>   }
>   sigma_tx_x_study ~ dt(0,pow(0.5,-2),1) T(0,)
> 
>   sigma_resid ~ dt(0,pow(0.5,-2),1) T(0,)
>   sigma2_resid <- sigma_resid*sigma_resid
>   sigma_study <- tau
> 
>   # Absolute level at the phase mean follow-up, retained for downstream output.
>   for (k in 1:n_tx) {
>     alpha[k] <- nh_mean_at_mean_weeks + tx_effect[k]
>     dev_nh[k] <- tx_effect[k]
>     dev_nh_26wk[k] <- tx_effect[k]  # LEGACY VARIABLE NAME; acute semantics = 26 wk
>     dev_nh_54wk[k] <- tx_effect[k]
>     dev_nh_52wk[k] <- tx_effect[k]  # compatibility alias only; not the chronic manuscript horizon
>   }
> }
> "
> prep_data <- function(raw, nh_params, condition) {
> 
>   # Grand-SD standardization at the raw row level.
>   # The authoritative analytic observation is study x T6 x weeks of observation.
>   # When multiple source rows map to the same observation (e.g. two arms collapsed
>   # to the same T6 category), their standardized changes are combined by inverse-
>   # variance weighting and their sample sizes are summed.
>   dat0 <- raw %>%
>     mutate(
>       b  = as.numeric(baseline),
>       s2 = as.numeric(score2),
>       n  = as.numeric(.data$n),
>       weeks = as.numeric(weeks),
>       treatment_type = canonical_treatment(treatment_type),
>       T6_key = derive_t6(T6, treatment_type),
>       scale = case_when(
>         b > 0  & b <= 10  ~ "NRS",
>         b > 10 & b <= 100 ~ "VAS",
>         TRUE              ~ NA_character_
>       ),
>       grand_sd = case_when(scale == "NRS" ~ SD_NRS,
>                            scale == "VAS" ~ SD_VAS,
>                            TRUE           ~ NA_real_),
>       J  = 1 - 3 / (4 * (n - 1) - 1),
>       g  = J * (b - s2) / grand_sd,
>       var_g = 1/n + g^2/(2*n),
>       ivw = ifelse(is.finite(var_g) & var_g > 0, 1/var_g, NA_real_)
>     ) %>%
>     dplyr::filter(!is.na(g), is.finite(g), !is.na(ivw), ivw > 0,
>                   (is.na(smd_method) | tolower(trimws(as.character(smd_method))) != "probit"),
>                   !is.na(weeks), !is.na(study), !is.na(T6_key), !is.na(treatment_type))
> 
>   first_nonblank <- function(x, default=NA_character_) {
>     z <- as.character(x)
>     z <- z[!is.na(z) & trimws(z) != ""]
>     if (!length(z)) default else z[1]
>   }
>   collapse_provider <- function(x, treatment) {
>     if (first_nonblank(treatment, "") != "SMT") return("none")
>     z <- unique(as.character(x[!is.na(x) & trimws(as.character(x)) != ""]))
>     if (!length(z)) return("Mixed")
>     if (length(z) == 1) return(z[1])
>     "Mixed"
>   }
> 
>   dat <- dat0 %>%
>     group_by(study, T6_key, weeks) %>%
>     summarise(
>       n = sum(n, na.rm=TRUE),
>       g = sum(g * ivw, na.rm=TRUE) / sum(ivw, na.rm=TRUE),
>       se = sqrt(1 / sum(ivw, na.rm=TRUE)),
>       treatment_type = first_nonblank(treatment_type),
>       smt_provider = collapse_provider(smt_provider, treatment_type),
>       quality_score = if ("quality_score" %in% names(dat0)) mean(as.numeric(quality_score), na.rm=TRUE) else NA_real_,
>       source_rows = dplyr::n(),
>       .groups="drop"
>     ) %>%
>     mutate(quality_score = ifelse(is.nan(quality_score), NA_real_, quality_score))
> 
>   # Audit the authoritative observation-key collapse.
>   if (any(dat$source_rows > 1)) {
>     cat(sprintf("  %s: collapsed %d source rows into %d study x T6 x week observations (%d observation keys had >1 source row).\n",
>                 condition, nrow(dat0), nrow(dat), sum(dat$source_rows > 1)))
>   }
> 
>   # Winsorize the aggregated observation effect at mean +/- 3 SD.
>   g_mean <- mean(dat$g); g_sd <- sd(dat$g)
>   dat <- dat %>% mutate(g_wins = pmin(pmax(g, g_mean - 3*g_sd), g_mean + 3*g_sd))
> 
>   tx_levels <- c("Control","SMT","Medical","Exercise","Modalities","Self_care")
> 
>   # Random-effect unit = study. Multi-site trials that have been deliberately
>   # parsed into site-specific study IDs (e.g. Goertz_2018a/b/c) therefore enter
>   # as separate study units. trial_random_id remains provenance metadata only;
>   # no parent-trial variance component is estimated.
>   dat <- dat %>%
>     mutate(
>       tx_int = as.integer(factor(treatment_type, levels=tx_levels)),
>       study_int = as.integer(factor(study))
>     ) %>%
>     dplyr::filter(!is.na(tx_int), !is.na(study_int))
> 
>   smt_prov_levels <- c("none","PT","DC","DO","MD","Bonesetters","Mixed")
>   dat <- dat %>%
>     mutate(
>       is_smt = as.integer(treatment_type == "SMT"),
>       smt_prov_label = case_when(
>         treatment_type != "SMT" ~ "none",
>         is.na(smt_provider) | smt_provider == "" ~ "Mixed",
>         TRUE ~ smt_provider
>       ),
>       smt_prov_int = as.integer(factor(smt_prov_label, levels=smt_prov_levels)),
>       smt_prov_int = ifelse(is.na(smt_prov_int), 1L, as.integer(smt_prov_int))
>     )
> 
>   n_obs    <- nrow(dat)
>   n_study  <- n_distinct(dat$study)
>   mean_wks <- mean(dat$weeks)
> 
>   size_c <- as.numeric(scale(log(dat$n + 1)))
>   pedro_c <- as.numeric(scale(as.numeric(dat$quality_score)))
>   pedro_c[is.na(pedro_c)] <- 0
> 
>   nh_m <- nh_params$mat
>   nh_one <- function(tt) {
>     xx <- nh_g_draws(nh_params, tt)
>     c(mean=mean(xx), var=var(xx))
>   }
>   nh_mv <- t(vapply(dat$weeks, nh_one, numeric(2)))
>   nh_mean <- as.numeric(nh_mv[,"mean"])
>   nh_var  <- pmax(as.numeric(nh_mv[,"var"]), 1e-10)
> 
>   xx_mean_t <- nh_g_draws(nh_params, mean_wks)
>   nh_mean_at_mean_weeks <- mean(xx_mean_t)
> 
>   list(
>     y=dat$g_wins, se=dat$se, weeks=dat$weeks, tx=dat$tx_int,

>     study=dat$study_int,

>     nh_mat=nh_params$mat, nh_info=nh_params,

> run_nma <- function(jd, label,
>                     n_chains = 4, n_adapt = 3000,
>                     n_burnin = 25000, n_iter = 100000, thin = 4,
>                     psrf_target = 1.01,
>                     max_retries = 2,
>                     retry_burnin = 25000,
>                     retry_iter = 200000) {
> 
>   cat(sprintf("\n=== %s BAYESIAN NMA ===\n", label))
>   cat(sprintf("  N observations: %d   N studies: %d   mean weeks: %.1f\n",
>               jd$N, jd$n_study, jd$mean_weeks))
>   cat(sprintf("  NH external posterior (%s): g_NH(0)=%.4f  rise=%.4f  lambda=%s\n",
>               if (is.null(jd$nh_info$source)) "0n" else jd$nh_info$source,
>               jd$nh_g0_mu, jd$nh_A_mu,
>               if (is.na(jd$nh_lam_mu)) "n/a (v21 log-time model)" else sprintf("%.5f", jd$nh_lam_mu)))
>   cat(sprintf("  Mean pointwise NH SD across observations: %.4f\n", mean(sqrt(jd$nh_var))))
> 
>   # Diagnostics — catch bad indices before JAGS sees them.
>   cat(sprintf("  smt_prov range: %d-%d  NAs: %d\n",
>               min(jd$smt_prov), max(jd$smt_prov), sum(is.na(jd$smt_prov))))
>   cat(sprintf("  is_smt: %d SMT observations, %d non-SMT\n",
>               sum(jd$is_smt), sum(!jd$is_smt)))
>   cat(sprintf("  tx range: %d-%d  NAs: %d\n",
>               min(jd$tx), max(jd$tx), sum(is.na(jd$tx))))
>   stopifnot(all(!is.na(jd$smt_prov)), all(!is.na(jd$tx)),
>             all(!is.na(jd$is_smt)), all(!is.na(jd$study)))
> 
>   jags_data <- jd[!names(jd) %in% c(
>     "tx_levels","prov_levels","dat","nh_A_sd","nh_lam_sd","nh_g0_sd","nh_mat",
>     "nh_info","nh_g0_mu","nh_A_mu","nh_lam_mu"
>   )]
> 
>   inits <- lapply(1:n_chains, function(i) list(
>     tx_effect    = rnorm(jd$n_tx, 0, 0.1),
>     z_gamma      = rnorm(jd$n_smt_prov, 0, 1),
>     sigma_tx     = runif(1, 0.1, 0.4),
>     sigma_prov   = runif(1, 0.05, 0.3),
>     tau          = runif(1, 0.3, 0.8),
>     beta_n       = rnorm(1, 0, 0.05),
>     beta_q       = rnorm(1, 0, 0.05),
>     u            = rnorm(jd$n_study, 0, 0.1),
>     sigma_resid      = runif(1, 0.10, 0.30),
>     sigma_tx_x_study = runif(1, 0.05, 0.20),
>     z_v              = matrix(rnorm(jd$n_tx * jd$n_study, 0, 1),
>                               jd$n_tx, jd$n_study)
>   ))
> 
>   model <- jags.model(
>     textConnection(model_string),
>     data     = jags_data,
>     inits    = inits,
>     n.chains = n_chains,
>     n.adapt  = n_adapt,
>     quiet    = FALSE
>   )
> 
>   params <- c(
>     "alpha", "tx_effect", "dev_nh", "dev_nh_26wk", "dev_nh_54wk", "dev_nh_52wk",
>     "gamma", "z_gamma", "sigma_prov",
>     "sigma_tx", "tau",
>     "sigma_study", "sigma_resid", "sigma_tx_x_study",
>     "beta_n", "beta_q"
>   )
> 
>   # Convergence helper used both for the initial sample and retry samples.
>   convergence_snapshot <- function(samps) {
>     gr <- tryCatch(
>       coda::gelman.diag(samps, multivariate=FALSE, autoburnin=FALSE)$psrf,
>       error=function(e) NULL
>     )
>     if (is.null(gr)) return(list(max_psrf=Inf, worst=NA_character_, min_ess=NA_real_))
>     ps <- as.numeric(gr[,1])
>     names(ps) <- rownames(gr)
>     ess <- tryCatch(as.numeric(coda::effectiveSize(samps)), error=function(e) NA_real_)
>     list(
>       max_psrf=max(ps, na.rm=TRUE),
>       worst=names(ps)[which.max(ps)],
>       min_ess=if (all(is.na(ess))) NA_real_ else min(ess, na.rm=TRUE)
>     )
>   }
> 
>   cat(sprintf("  Burn-in: %d iterations...\n", n_burnin))
>   update(model, n_burnin)
> 
>   cat(sprintf("  Sampling: %d iterations (thin=%d)...\n", n_iter, thin))
>   samples <- coda.samples(model, params, n.iter=n_iter, thin=thin)
>   cv <- convergence_snapshot(samples)
>   cat(sprintf("  Initial fresh-sample max PSRF = %.4f for %s; min ESS = %s\n",
>               cv$max_psrf,
>               ifelse(is.na(cv$worst), "NA", cv$worst),
>               ifelse(is.na(cv$min_ess), "NA", format(round(cv$min_ess), big.mark=","))))
> 
>   # IMPORTANT: do not relax the prespecified convergence gate. If the first
>   # fresh sample narrowly misses it, extend warm-up and draw a NEW fresh sample.
>   # This mirrors the successful retry strategy used in the authoritative NH model.
>   retry <- 0L
>   while (is.finite(cv$max_psrf) && cv$max_psrf > psrf_target && retry < max_retries) {
>     retry <- retry + 1L
>     cat(sprintf(
>       "  Retry %d/%d: max PSRF %.4f > %.2f; extra burn-in %d, then fresh sampling %d (thin=%d)...\n",
>       retry, max_retries, cv$max_psrf, psrf_target, retry_burnin, retry_iter, thin
>     ))
>     update(model, retry_burnin)
>     samples <- coda.samples(model, params, n.iter=retry_iter, thin=thin)
>     cv <- convergence_snapshot(samples)
>     cat(sprintf("  Retry %d fresh-sample max PSRF = %.4f for %s; min ESS = %s\n",
>                 retry, cv$max_psrf,
>                 ifelse(is.na(cv$worst), "NA", cv$worst),
>                 ifelse(is.na(cv$min_ess), "NA", format(round(cv$min_ess), big.mark=","))))
>   }
> 
>   if (is.finite(cv$max_psrf) && cv$max_psrf > psrf_target) {
>     cat(sprintf(
>       "  Convergence retry exhausted: max PSRF %.4f for %s remains above %.2f.\n",
>       cv$max_psrf, cv$worst, psrf_target
>     ))
>   } else {
>     cat(sprintf("  Convergence retry gate passed: max PSRF %.4f <= %.2f.\n",
>                 cv$max_psrf, psrf_target))
>   }
> 
>   list(samples=samples, jd=jd, label=label,
>        convergence=cv, convergence_retries=retry)
> }
> format_table <- function(result, condition) {
>   samps <- result$samples
>   jd    <- result$jd
>   label <- result$label
>   mat   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(samps, as.matrix))
> 
>   smry <- function(par_name, display_name = NULL) {
>     if (!par_name %in% colnames(mat)) return(NULL)
>     x    <- mat[, par_name]
>     psrf <- tryCatch(
>       gelman.diag(samps[, par_name, drop=FALSE],
>                   multivariate=FALSE)$psrf[1,1],
>       error = function(e) NA)
>     ess_b <- tryCatch(
>       effectiveSize(samps[, par_name, drop=FALSE]),
>       error = function(e) NA)
>     ess_t <- tryCatch({
>       half <- ceiling(length(x)/2)
>       min(effectiveSize(samps[, par_name, drop=FALSE][half:length(x)]), NA)
>     }, error = function(e) NA)
>     data.frame(
>       Variable = if (!is.null(display_name)) display_name else par_name,
>       Mean     = round(mean(x),            3),
>       Median   = round(median(x),          3),
>       SD       = round(sd(x),              3),
>       MAD      = round(mad(x),             3),
>       CI_2.5   = round(quantile(x, 0.025), 3),
>       CI_97.5  = round(quantile(x, 0.975), 3),
>       PSRF     = round(psrf,               4),
>       ESS_Bulk = round(ess_b,              0),
>       stringsAsFactors = FALSE
>     )
>   }
> 
>   hdr <- function(txt)
>     data.frame(Variable=txt, Mean=NA, Median=NA, SD=NA, MAD=NA,

> 
>   rows <- list()

>   }
>   ext_time <- function(lbl,t) ext_param(lbl, nh_g_draws(jd$nh_info, t))
> 
>   nstud <- if (condition=="acute") {

>     as.integer(jd$nh_info$n_studies)
>   }
>   rows[["h2"]] <- hdr(sprintf(
>     "=== NATURAL HISTORY (EXTERNAL BAYESIAN HIERARCHICAL NH; %d STUDIES; POINTWISE UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATED) ===",

>   if (identical(jd$nh_info$source, "v21")) {

>   if (condition != "acute")

>   rows[["sig_tx"]]  <- smry("sigma_tx",     "sigma_tx (treatment spread around NH)")
> 
>   rows[["h3"]]  <- hdr("=== TREATMENTS (grand-SD standardized g) ===")

> summ_pp <- function(x) {
>   x <- x[is.finite(x)]
>   if (!length(x)) return(tibble(mean=NA_real_,lo=NA_real_,hi=NA_real_))

>     mean=mean(x),

> build_phase <- function(phase,horizon,seed) {
>   z <- phase_draws(phase,horizon,seed)
>   m <- z$m
>   gnh <- z$gnh
>   ex <- z$ex
> 
>   DEFS <- if (phase=="Acute") DEFS_ACUTE else DEFS_CHRONIC
> 
>   map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(DEFS)), function(i) {
>     dd <- DEFS$delta[i]
> 
>     # Paired Control probability for every posterior draw.
>     p_control <- pnorm(gnh + ex*m[,"Control"] - dd)
> 
>     map_dfr(TX_ACTIVE,function(tx) {
>       p_tx <- pnorm(gnh + ex*m[,tx] - dd)
> 
>       # Draw-by-draw risk difference, expressed as extra recoveries / 100.
>       diff_pp <- 100 * (p_tx - p_control)
> 
>       summ_pp(diff_pp) %>%
>         mutate(
>           Treatment=tx,
>           Phase=phase,
>           definition=DEFS$definition[i],
>           def_index=DEFS$def_index[i]
>         )
>     })
>   })
> }

> panel_benefit <- function(d,title) {
>   d <- droplevels(d)
> 
>   # Shared phase-specific y range with generous padding.
>   ymin <- min(d$lo,na.rm=TRUE)
>   ymax <- max(d$hi,na.rm=TRUE)
>   yrng <- ymax-ymin
>   pad  <- max(3,0.12*yrng)
>   ylo  <- floor((ymin-pad)/5)*5
>   yhi  <- 30
> 
>   phase_value <- as.character(unique(d$Phase))
>   ax <- axis_tbl %>%
>     filter(Treatment %in% unique(d$Treatment))
> 
>   labs_under <- tx_layout %>%
>     filter(Treatment %in% unique(d$Treatment))
> 
>   ggplot(
>     d,
>     aes(x=xpos,y=mean,color=Treatment,group=Treatment)
>   ) +
>     geom_hline(
>       yintercept=0,
>       linetype="dashed",
>       color="grey30",
>       linewidth=.65
>     ) +
>     geom_vline(
>       xintercept=separators,
>       linetype="dotted",
>       color="grey82",
>       linewidth=.45
>     ) +
> 
>     # CAPPED 95% credible intervals.
>     # width controls the tiny horizontal cross-lines at top and bottom.
>     geom_errorbar(
>       aes(ymin=lo,ymax=hi),
>       width=.22,
>       linewidth=.72,
>       alpha=.95
>     ) +
> 
>     geom_line(
>       linewidth=.95
>     ) +
>     geom_point(

>     ) +
>

>     geom_text(
>       data=labs_under,
>       aes(
>         x=group_center,
>         y=ylo - 0.11*(yhi-ylo),

> d <- raw %>%
>   mutate(b = as.numeric(baseline), s2 = as.numeric(score2), n = as.numeric(.data$n),
>          grand_sd = case_when(b > 0 & b <= 10 ~ SD_NRS,
>                               b > 10 & b <= 100 ~ SD_VAS, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
>          J  = 1 - 3/(4*(n-1) - 1),
>          g  = J * (b - s2) / grand_sd,

> abc <- function(phase,wk,delta) {
>   d <- canonical_clinical_draws(canon,phase,wk,delta)
>   map_dfr(TX_LEVELS,function(tx) {
>     p <- d$p[,tx]; cdraw <- 100*(p-d$p_control)
>     tibble(Condition=phase,Treatment=tx,week=wk,delta=delta,
>            A=100*mean(p),
>            B=100*mean(p-d$p_nh),
>            C=mean(cdraw),
>            C_lo=unname(quantile(cdraw,.025)),
>            C_hi=unname(quantile(cdraw,.975)))
>   })
> }
> defs <- bind_rows(
>   map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(DEFS_ACUTE)),function(i) abc("Acute",WK_AC,DEFS_ACUTE$delta[i]) %>% mutate(definition=DEFS_ACUTE$definition[i])),
>   map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(DEFS_CHRONIC)),function(i) abc("Chronic",WK_CH,DEFS_CHRONIC$delta[i]) %>% mutate(definition=DEFS_CHRONIC$definition[i]))
> ) %>% mutate(
>   Condition=factor(Condition,levels=c("Acute","Chronic")),
>   Treatment=factor(Treatment,levels=TX_LEVELS),
>   definition=factor(definition,levels=DEFS_ACUTE$definition),
>   NNT=ifelse(C>0.05,100/C,NA_real_))
> out1 <- defs %>% transmute(Condition,definition,Treatment,delta,
>   `A recovered per 100`=sprintf("%.1f",A),
>   `B extra vs NH`=sprintf("%+.1f",B),
>   `C extra vs control`=sprintf("%+.1f",C),
>   `C 95% CI`=sprintf("[%+.1f, %+.1f]",C_lo,C_hi),
>   NNT=ifelse(is.na(NNT),"-",sprintf("%.0f",NNT)))
> write_csv(out1,"Table_15_recovery_definitions.csv")
> cat("✓ Table_15_recovery_definitions.csv\n")

Some reported values were only found alongside OTHER components after being separated from their own originally-reported neighbours (e.g. a mean split from its own confidence interval). The “Plausible” column marks whether that split is well-supported: TRUE when the pieces still trace back to the same underlying variable (via the output’s own row labels), FALSE when no such link was found — a FALSE match is not necessarily wrong, but is worth checking against its own Source file/Analysis columns before treating it as confirmed.
